Risk officer assessment, Reelpad (age 30.6 min, class ORGANIC, alive):

Recommendation: refuse, or at most a $5 ticket if the desk insists. Reasons:

- Pool depth is 190 SOL, adequate, but the last 15 minutes show heavy two-way churn: $315k volume, 1,262 sellers against 1,668 buyers, sell-to-buy ratio near 0.88 right after graduation, and a -14% return. Net flow is only +12.8 SOL on 1,308 SOL bought, so this is distribution-like churn, not accumulation.
- It already sits 32% below its 30-minute high, after a 2.46x run. That is a fresh post-pump drawdown in a coin that sold off hard, the pattern where most coins never recover.
- The launch-bot presence and 477 early buyers mean the "organic" label is fragile.

If the desk buys anyway: $5 ticket, 20% stop, 15-minute hold, and exit at once if the pool drops below roughly 150 SOL. Do not size up.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying Reelpad now is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping.

What supports it: the coin is classed ORGANIC, with no airdrop dump seen, a low curve bundle share (4.4%), and top-3 curve holders at only 8.2%. Buyer count is high (554 on the curve, 1,668 in the last 15 minutes), and the first two minutes after graduation saw 477 buyers ex-agent with 536 SOL of buying. The pool depth of 190 SOL is reasonable for a $20 ticket.

What argues against it: net flow over the last 15 minutes is essentially flat (+12.8 SOL on 1,308 SOL of buys), the price is down 14% in that window, and it is 32% off its 30-minute high. The sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.88, and a launch bot was present. Last-15-minute sellers (1,262) nearly match buyers (1,668), so the demand that built the 2.46x run is being matched by exit liquidity. Position is 30.6 minutes old, inside the window where recent base rates have been unkind, and it is already in drawdown rather than stabilizing. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost also means it needs a meaningful move just to break even.

Verdict: no strong case for demand persisting 30-60 minutes. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: distribution into the drawdown. The coin is up 2.46x over 30 minutes but has already fallen 32% from its high, and the last 15 minutes show -14% return with sell SOL (1,295.56) nearly matching buy SOL (1,308.36), net flow only +12.8 SOL. Sellers (1,262) outnumber the buyer count of the window by a wide margin relative to the flow, and sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.88, so early buyers were already exiting. Pool depth is only 190 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leaves little room: a further 10-15% slide at this depth would erase any bounce. Volume looks large, but it is churn, not conviction. Skip.
